title: user-confirmation-detector.ts (UserPromptSubmit hot path) passes the raw user prompt into an execSync shell:true command escaping only " — backtick/$()/;/> in a prompt reaches the shell (command injection + junk creation)
observe_how: Two call sites build content embedding the user's verbatim prompt (`User confirmed: "${prompt}"`) and exec it with execSync({shell:true}), escaping only the double-quote (`.replace(/"/g, '\\"')`) — NOT backtick, $(), ;, &, > or %VAR%. This is a UserPromptSubmit hook so the prompt is fully user-controlled free text. A prompt containing a backtick or $(...) executes an arbitrary subcommand; a > redirects store_learning stdout to an attacker/user-named file. Same remediation: spawnSync with an args array, drop shell:true. (Note: on Windows the execSync shell is cmd.exe, where \" is NOT a valid quote-escape anyway, so even the one escape applied is ineffective — a literal " in a prompt breaks --content quoting regardless.)
telemetry: Log when a prompt reaching storeUserConfirmedLearning/storeVictoryFromConfirmation contains shell metacharacters; count resulting non-zero store exits.
